title: Orion dedicated capacity playtest and commitment scenarios
content:
Summary:
This note captures the playtest-oriented sizing proposals and autoscale guardrails we sketched during the Orion workshop (Nov 2024). Focus: reduce burst costs while preserving 95th pct latency SLO=250ms for chat endpoints and keep predictable monthly committed spend for their compliance team.

Customer context and traffic profile (as reported by Orion):
- Product: internal knowledge-assistant (chat+search) used by support agents.
- Expected daily active users (DAU) during trial: 2,500.
- Peak concurrent sessions (90th): 320.
- Typical session pattern: short prompts (80 tokens) + generative replies (~140 tokens).
- Target SLO: p95 < 250ms for generation-first token; p95 end-to-end < 700ms (including routing).

Key modeling assumptions for sizing (conservative and transparent):
- Model choice for baseline tests: "rw-instruct-13b-q4" (4-bit quantized 13B family).
- Effective tokens processed per request = prompt + response = 220 tokens on average.
- Baseline per-GPU throughput (measured in local experiments with similar models): ~45 requests/sec for 13B q4 under mixed prompt lengths and streaming enabled (batching enabled with 40ms aggregation). This is a conservative lab estimate for H100-class nodes with optimized kernels.
- Warm KV cache hit rate target (after priming): 25% (saves ~40% compute for repeated prompt prefixes).

Instance economics (assumptions for committed/dedicated pool):
- H100-80GB equivalent (committed reserved price assumed): $9.00 / GPU-hour (includes infra overhead and reserved discount).
- H100 on-demand: $14.00 / GPU-hour (used only for short bursts / overflow).
- Small fallback instance (A10-like / 80GB mixed): $3.50 / GPU-hour (for rw-instruct-7b fallbacks).

Quick cost math examples (baseline numbers):
- Per-GPU capacity: 45 req/s => 162,000 req/hr.
- Cost per request (committed H100): $9.00 / 162,000 = $0.0000556 (~0.0056c).
- Cost per 1k requests: $0.0556.
- Monthly cost (720h) per GPU: 720 * $9 = $6,480.

Three commitment scenarios (recommended for workshop discussion):
1) Foot-in-the-door (low-commit)
   - Reserved pool: 1 H100 + 0 burst on-demand
   - Steady throughput capacity: ~45 req/s (p50 throughput)
   - Monthly committed cost: $6,480
   - Risks: saturated at modest peak, relies heavily on autoscale to on-demand which increases marginal cost.

2) Standard trial (recommended)
   - Reserved pool: 3 H100 (min pool) + 2 H100 on-demand burst slots allowed
   - Effective steady capacity: ~135 req/s; peak headroom (with burst) ~225 req/s
   - Monthly committed cost: 3 * $6,480 = $19,440 (predictable)
   - Expected p95 latency headroom for baseline workloads; can absorb short spikes with 2 on-demand GPUs.

3) Enterprise pilot (aggressive)
   - Reserved pool: 8 H100 + 4 on-demand burst
   - Monthly committed cost: 8 * $6,480 = $51,840
   - Rationale: for customers who want predictable multi-user SLA across regions and 99.9 uptime.

Autoscale and guardrail proposal (playtest-ready):
- Metrics used for decisions: GPU compute utilization (aggregate), avg queue depth (requests waiting to be scheduled), tail token latency (p95 token generation), and cold-start counts.
- Scale-out triggers (fast path):
  - If queue depth > 40 sustained for >90s -> add 1 GPU (on-demand until pool grows).
  - If GPU utilization > 72% sustained for 120s -> add 1 GPU.
  - If p95 token latency > 300ms and queue depth > 10 -> add 1 GPU.
- Scale-in triggers (conservative):
  - If GPU utilization < 42% for 5 minutes AND queue depth == 0 -> remove 1 on-demand GPU.
  - Only scale-in reserved pool capacity at weekly windows (to avoid churn affecting committed billing); for reserved pool changes use change window ops via sales.
- Prewarm and headroom policy:
  - Maintain 20% warm headroom during business hours (08:00-20:00 local) by prewarming a standby GPU; headroom enforcement only for reserved pool (reduces burst to on-demand).
- Cooldowns and rate limits: 10m cooldown between scale operations to avoid oscillation; cap of +2 GPUs per 10 minutes.

Fallback and graceful degradation strategy:
- When sustained overflow > 6 minutes and on-demand capacity exhausted, route excess requests to cheaper rw-instruct-7b instances with best-effort fidelity (explicitly record fallback in response headers for observability).
- For extreme overload (>1800 queued requests), enable degraded response mode: trim generation max_tokens by 30% and disable long-form evidence retrieval to preserve latency.

Benchmark plan (playtest steps):
1) Lab synthetic ramp (solutions-eng): run open-source loadgen against rw-instruct-13b-q4 on 1,3, and 8 GPU pools to validate throughput/latency curves. Capture per-token CPU/GPU breakdown.
2) KV cache priming run: pre-populate typical prompt prefixes and measure hit-rate improvements and latency impact.
3) Spike tests: 10x sudden spiky bursts for 30s/5m durations to validate autoscale reaction and on-demand integration.
4) Long soak: 48h steady-state run at 60% avg utilization to spot memory leaks and queue behavior.
5) Failure injection: Simulate one GPU node flapping to verify graceful fallback and request retry behavior.

Open questions / items for customer alignment:
- Commitment window: do they prefer monthly reserved billing or 12-month? (affects discounts we can offer; present both options in follow-up).
- Which regions matter? We recommended starting in us-west2 and eu-west1; if they need APAC we should add a warm standby in ap-south1 (cost +$1k/month).
- Data residency and logging retention: trial default is 30 days; enterprise may require 365 days which affects storage costs and audit windows.
- Acceptance criteria for pilot: target p95 latency, <0.5% fallback rate to 7B, and monthly cost variance <10% vs projection.

Operational runbook snippets (for solutions-eng + SRE handoff):
- On-call runbook: if reserved pool GPU drops below min nodes -> immediate page oncall-sre and engage SE to enable rapid on-demand expansion.
- Cost alerting: if on-demand spend > 15% of committed spend for 3 consecutive days -> trigger customer-facing escalation and review.
- Observability: dashboard tiles to include token/sec, req/sec, queue depth, p95 generation latency, fallback-rate, and headroom %.

Next steps (for the week):
- [Asha] finalize baseline lab scripts and benchmark harness by Nov 20.
- [Jonah] prepare pricing comparison matrix for monthly vs 12-month commit and draft a short customer-facing one-pager.
- [Elena] schedule customer walkthrough with Orion infra/security for data residency checklist.
- [Marcus] instrument loadgen to emit trace headers that map to Orion session ids.

Appendix: quick sensitivity table (rounded):
- Single H100 (committed): $6,480/month -> supports ~162k req/hr -> ~3.9M req/month.
- Cost per 100k requests ~ $5.56.
- If KV cache improves hit-rate from 0% to 25% -> effective req/sec increases by ~20-30% for repeated prompt patterns -> could reduce committed GPUs by 1 in mid-sizes.

Notes and unresolved discussion points (workshop artifacts):
- Customer asked about quantization safety for legal-domain answers; need to validate answer fidelity on their eval promptset (Action: add to bench run).
- They asked for a simple SLA doc: draft to be produced by Product.

End of playtest draft.

(Informal/notes-to-self):
- Consider shipping a tiny sample dashboard showing cost vs latency trade-offs for their exec deck.
- Keep the initial commit small; customers often underestimate burst Vs steady and overspend in on-demand.
